text:
Rae M: quick thread 10k bring-up for pelican12 (12B). experiment: int6 default + cheap prefix-cache + confidence-triggered rerank (only rerank low-confidence outputs) + dynamic temp-anneal. goal: recover quality while keeping unit econ. results below.

Tom S: love the combo. top-line numbers first pls.

Rae M: eval-bot summary pasted: sample_n=10000, baseline=all-int8, alt=hybrid-int6+cache+conf-rerank, cost_delta=-34% vs int8, QA_acc_delta=-0.9pp, hallucination_delta=+0.7pp, rerank_trigger_rate=9.8%, cache_hit=27%, p95_latency_delta=+9ms (mostly when rerank triggers)

eval-bot: summary: cost_change=-34%, qa_acc_change=-0.9pp, halluc_change=+0.7pp, rerank_rate=9.8%, cache_hit=27%, p95+9ms, n=10000

Lena K: nice. how does the rerank/rewarm flow work?

Rae M: flow: default serve int6. if confidence_score < threshold -> generate N=3 candidates int6, rerank them with a cheap discriminative scorer (distilled 1.2M) and optionally rescore top candidate with int8 logits-only re-eval (not full decode) if rerank_confidence still low. cache stores prefix->token-stream for repeated prompts (cosine>0.985) to short-circuit. temperature anneal: reduce temp by 0.15 for low-confidence cases before rerank to tighten outputs.

Tom S: table of rounded numbers we used:
```
variant                             cost_per_1k  QA_acc  halluc_rate  p95_latency  notes
pelican12-int8-baseline             $0.88        83.9%   2.4%         220ms        all-int8
pelican12-hybrid-int6+cache+conf    $0.58        83.0%   3.1%         229ms        int6 default, 9.8% rerank
```

Priya R: what's the effective cost_per_1k accounting for rerank triggers and cache hits?

Rae M: effective cost_per_1k ~= $0.58 using trace assumptions (cache_hit=27%, rerank_trigger=9.8%). quick calc assumes rerank cost ~+8% on those triggered requests and int8 re-eval +2% of triggered outputs.

Rae M: unit-econ for GTN (assume avg tokens/req=1.5k):
- baseline all-int8: cost_per_1k=$0.88 -> cost_per_req ~= $1.32 -> per_1M_req ~= $1,320
- hybrid: effective cost_per_1k=$0.58 -> cost_per_req ~= $0.87 -> per_1M_req ~= $870
- savings ~= $450 per 1M requests (~34.1%)

Lena K: good hit. where are quality regressions concentrated?

Rae M: concentrated on long abstractive summarization and highly creative/ambiguous prompts. Confidence head precision on true failures ~75% at the chosen threshold. rerank recovers ~1.1pp of QA and reduces halluc by ~1.6pp within the triggered slice. int8 logits-only re-eval cuts the remaining halluc by ~0.6pp but adds ~2% unit cost overall if enabled for all triggered cases.

Tom S: sim command used:
```bash
python tools/sim_hybrid.py \
  --trace traces/mix_webchat_10k.json \
  --policy "int6_default;cache_thresh=0.985;conf_thresh=0.38;rerank_n=3;temp_anneal= -0.15;int8_rescore=on" \
  --metrics cost,qa_acc,halluc_rate,rerank_rate,cache_hit,p95 \
  --out reports/pelican12_hybrid_3627777001.json
```

Priya R: product/GTN question: recommended rollout and guardrails?

Rae M: recommendation: staged rollout with tight controls. Start 3% canary -> 20% over 12 days. Gate signals: absolute hallucination_rate > 4% or delta on priority QA slices > 2pp or rerank_trigger_rate deviates >5pp from sim or cache_hit drops >10pp. Fallback: revert routing to all-int8 or temporarily increase conf threshold to reduce rerank coverage.

Lena K: ops needs: billing tag per variant, metrics: rerank_trigger_rate, cache_hit, per-slice hallucination, p95, and per-variant spend. Also alert: hallucination>4% sustained 5m OR rerank_rate>20% sustained 10m.

Tom S: mitigation knobs: 1) raise conf threshold (reduces rerank triggers, lowers cost downside to base int6 but increases quality risk), 2) enable int8 logits-only rescore selectively for top-5 failure triggers, 3) route >2500 token requests to int8 directly, 4) enable rerank only on top-n granular slices (abstractive only).

Priya R: can you craft a one-paragraph GTN blurb with unit econ? need customer-safe language.

Rae M: draft exec blurb: "Recommend piloting a cost-first hybrid for pelican12: int6 as the default with a small prefix cache and a confidence-triggered rerank flow that selectively escalates to higher-cost evaluation only when outputs are low-confidence. In simulation this approach reduced model spend by ~34% while keeping net QA and hallucination within product guardrails; rerank triggers were under 10% of requests and focused on abstractive longform cases. Start with a 3% canary, widen to 20% with strict gates on hallucination, QA-slice regressions, and trigger rates. If guardrails trip, revert to all-int8 until we investigate." 

eval-bot: artifacts uploaded -> s3://redwood-eval/pelican12/3627777001/ (includes per-slice CSV, top-200 failures, conf-calibration plot, and sim config)

Tom S: owners/actions:
- Rae: upload per-slice CSV, top-200 failures, threshold-cal plot, and the sim config (EOD).
- Lena/Ops: add billing tags and implement alerts + expose rerank_trigger metric in console.
- Priya: draft GTN playbook copy and confirm canary cadence (3->20).
- Tom: wire a lightweight smoke harness for canary to emit rerank_rate and per-slice hallucination hourly.

Lena K: will review infra implications for cache storage and re-eval compute.

Rae M: will follow up with the doc link and the raw CSV. ping when ready.

Priya R: thanks all, looks like a promising cost-quality compromise. :rocket:
